# `contact-schedule`

Scenario kind of the engine v0.38.0, family [Mission analysis, links and space operations](../mission-analysis-links-and-space-operations.md). Advisory: analysis output from a research and engineering tool, not type-approved navigation equipment and not a safety-of-life service. Every label here is the engine's or the verification matrix's; a kind is MODELLED unless the matrix says otherwise (how a label is earned: the README's Evidence section).

## What it does

Ground-contact planning for several satellites over several stations: apparent access windows (SGP4, IAU 2006/2000A Earth-fixed frame, ITU-R P.834 refraction, light time), the DVB-S2 ACM data volume of each pass (ETSI EN 302 307-1 Table 13 thresholds) and a conflict-free schedule (one satellite per antenna with a turnaround, one station per satellite, priority-weighted delivery capped at each backlog) by a marginal-value greedy, a first-come baseline and an exact branch and bound on small sets, with the greedy's optimality gap. MODELLED.

One run of `scenarios/contact-schedule.toml` summarises as: contact-schedule: 3 satellites x 3 stations over 12 h -> 31 candidate contacts, 22 scheduled; 797266 of 860000 Mbit delivered (MODELLED)
